To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DNA melting curve simulation software POLAND and MELSITM can be successfully used for the design of diagnostic assays that use intercalating d yes such as SYTO 9, but the simulation programs need to be refined to account for the effects of intercalating dye concentrations on melting profiles and that the complex melting profiles of PCR amplicon generated in vitro are solely the result of double-stranded DNA dissociation.

DNA melting simulation software is a useful tool for the design of real-time PCR assays that exploit complex melting curves and that the complex melting curve profiles observed in real-time PCR using double-stranded dye SYTO9 are solely the result of dissociation of the DNA.
DNA melting simulation software can be used to identify regions with diagnostic melting profiles, and that these regions are not limited to the Tm of single nucleotide polymorphisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of DNA melting simulation programs for diagnostic assay design, and the confirmation of the predicted melting profiles in vitro using intercalating dye.
the design of in silico DNA diagnostic assays using the melting curve analysis of PCR amplicon generated using double stranded DNA-specific intercalating d yes such as SYTO®9.
the use of DNA melting curve analysis for diagnostic purposes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

DNA melting simulation programs such as POLAND and MELSIM are a useful tool for in silico design of diagnostic assays, but further refinements to the software are required to accurately simulate melting in the presence of intercalating dye.
the POLAND and the MELTSIM programs are useful tools for the identification of diagnostic melting curve assay targets.
the DNA melting simulation programs POLAND and, to a lesser extent MELTSIM are valuable tools for the design of diagnostic melting curve assays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these DNA melting simulation programs are valuable tools to assist in the design of diagnostic assays that exploit the melting curve profiles of double stranded DNA.

the use of DNA melting simulation programs can be used to identify potential diagnostic melting curve assays, but that the programs should be used as a guide and that the melting profiles generated in silico should be compared with the profiles generated in vitro to confirm the melting domains that contribute to the melting peaks observed.

DNA melting simulations can be used to identify regions where complex melting profiles can be exploited for diagnostic assay design and that this is a valuable tool in the development of real-time PCR diagnostic assays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA melting simulation programs can provide useful information for the design of diagnostic assays that rely on DNA melting curve profiles.
the melting curve profiles of PCR products can be predicted in silico and the melting simulations can be used to identify regions where diagnostic melting curve assays can be developed.

the melting curve profiles generated in vitro with SYTO9 are the result of double stranded DNA dissociation and can be predicted with the simulation programs POLAND and, with the necessary refinements, MELTSIM.
